records.prose: While the application is loading, a centered message on a black screen displays “GRIDATLAS” in amber above “verifying immutable shell and cartridges…” in cyan. The completed page opens on a compact, dark dashboard. A narrow status strip spans the top, with the local time and date against the left edge, the Ventus wordmark and “Cables & Connectivity®” centered, and “2050 TARGET” against the right edge. The clock and date update once a second using British display formats. The target shows the whole number of days remaining to midnight UTC on 1 January 2050, rounded down, followed by “DAYS” in amber. The initial time, date and countdown positions show placeholders until the first update. The black page fills the visible window. The status strip, map, and lower layer panel form one column with a four-pixel outer inset and four-pixel gaps between panels. The map grows to use the remaining height above the layer panel, with a thin charcoal border and six-pixel rounded corners. The lower panel has a scrollable inset list. Its list uses two columns above 480 pixels wide and one column at 480 pixels and below. The lower panel can take up to 38 percent of the viewport height, dropping to 28 percent when the viewport is 600 pixels high or shorter.

records.evidence: Controlled prose-guided reconstruction of the map and Airports slice. Candidate frozen scores: 48/50 then 38/50, with two skips. Both original and revised candidate passed 50/50 visible-caption replay cases, including 12 held-out checks. The recorded accessible-name difference remains, and screen-reader announcement parity was not tested. Host read isolation was unavailable. The revised experiment used prose v3 with a separate dashboard geometry addendum. Stage 1 experiment receipt and scope: https://github.com/Ventusltd/neural-link-between-agents/issues/87#issuecomment-7201375567

records.prose: The view starts over Great Britain at longitude −3.5 degrees, latitude 54 degrees and zoom level 4.2. The dark base map is the default. Dragging across the map pans the view, and scrolling, pinching or double-clicking zooms it using the declared mapping library's normal map gestures. Ordinary map movement remains available while the layer is hidden and while its data is loading. Resizing the map panel updates the drawing surface. The base map for this experiment is the supplied frozen dark style. The original dark tiles and imagery services are outside this trial. With visible airport data from OpenStreetMap, give the dataset the visible credit “© OpenStreetMap contributors” and retain the credit when the layer is toggled.

records.prose:
The visible layer panel and the airport checkbox are separate controls. A dark button with pale teal text is fixed 12 pixels from the right and bottom edges of the window. It has a minimum size of 44 by 44 pixels and shows a two-pixel teal outline when focused by keyboard. On the first visit with a typical desktop pointer and a window wider than 700 pixels, the panel is open and the button reads “▾ HIDE LAYERS”. A coarse pointer, or a known positive window width of 700 pixels or less, starts with the panel closed and the button reads “▴ LAYERS”. Its accessible name is “Hide the layers panel” when open and “Show the layers panel” when closed. In ordinary view, the button reports itself as pressed when the panel is closed.

Clicking or tapping the button hides or restores the lower panel. The map stays in view and resizes to use the released space when the panel closes. Neither the camera position nor the airport checkbox changes when the panel closes. The most recent panel choice is remembered in that browser across page reloads and takes precedence over the first-visit rule. If the browser cannot save the choice, the control still works for the current visit. The 700-pixel first-visit rule is separate from the 480-pixel rule for laying out the list inside an open panel.

records.prose: In the layer panel, “Airports” appears as a magenta label in the “ASSETS (GEOJSON)” group alongside an ordinary checkbox. It starts unchecked. A keyboard user can use the usual tab-and-space behavior of the checkbox. Initially the caption reads “Airports [WAIT]”. Once the base map is ready, the application requests the airport points in the background even if the checkbox stays unchecked, and the caption changes to “Airports [LOAD]” while the request is in progress. The 15-second timer covers obtaining the HTTP response. Reading the body as JSON happens after that timer has been cleared. A readable feature collection with one or more entries makes the caption “Airports [OK]”. A successful response containing no entries, or a JSON object without a feature array, is treated as empty and displays “Airports [EMPTY]”. A request that fails or yields unreadable JSON displays “Airports [FAIL]”, with the caption at half opacity. Turning a failed layer off and back on can retry the request. An empty successful response is retained as loaded for that page visit.

records.prose: Each airport is supplied as a geographical point with longitude first and latitude second, in degrees. Once the points are ready and the checkbox is checked, the map draws them at those positions as magenta circles, color #ff00ff, with a radius of 4.5 screen pixels and a one-pixel black outline. They use that screen size at all zoom levels. The same frozen dataset is used the next time the layer is enabled in that visit. Unchecking the layer hides the points directly without moving the camera or discarding loaded data. A request may finish while the layer is hidden. When it finishes, the caption can become “[OK]” while the points stay hidden.

records.prose: With the airport layer visible and no special map tool active, hovering over a rendered point shows a pointer cursor. The original limits hover hit checks to about one every 100 milliseconds. Click or tap a rendered point to open an information popup at the clicked location. Its title is the airport's displayed name, in bright cyan bold 13-pixel monospace on a black background. If no name is available the fallback reads “Unnamed Asset”. In the supplied airport dataset the records carry a name only, so the popup displays the name with no invented airport type or details. Display names as ordinary text, including punctuation. The popup has a maximum width of 300 pixels and a close control. Opening a new one closes the previous popup. Hidden airports are unavailable for a new selection. Clicking empty map space opens no new popup. Dismiss the open popup using its close control or by clicking empty map space. Hiding the layer removes the markers from hit testing and does not itself close a popup that was already open.
